tasks.title: Read: DDIA Ch.9 — Consistency and Consensus

subtasks.text: Notes on linearisability vs. eventual consistency
Sketch how Raft relates to our dedup window TTL design

tasks.notes:
Aug 25: The Raft section crystallised a lot about distributed consensus that had been fuzzy. The single-leader replication failure modes map directly to what we're doing with Redis as the dedup window — we're trusting a single primary for linearisability.
Aug 27: The 'READ COMMITTED' analogy for Redis Cluster is useful. Worth a spike to validate the latency budget holds under cluster mode.

tasks.title: Spike: Redis Cluster mode for high-throughput dedup

subtasks.text: Hash slot distribution for composite dedup keys
Benchmark: single-shard vs. 6-shard cluster at 1.2M events/min

tasks.notes: Aug 28: Set up local 6-shard cluster. Hash slot assignment with {source} prefix keeps related keys co-located. Initial benchmark looks very promising — continuing in W36.

tasks.title: Spike: Redis Cluster mode for high-throughput dedup
tasks.notes:
Sep 1: 6-shard cluster breaks through the single-shard ceiling. 1.35M events/min at p99 18ms — comfortably inside the 20ms budget.
Sep 3: Spike write-up posted to PLAT-3918. Recommendation: adopt Redis Cluster for the production dedup engine. The {source}-prefixed hash slot strategy keeps related dedup keys co-located and avoids cross-slot scripting issues.
